observations: Photo 0: A complete automatic transmission assembly with torque converter attached, lying on paved/brick ground, with a watermark 'FIDEL AUTOS GLOBAL LIMITED'.
Photo 0: A white manufacturer sticker is visible on the transmission case but the printed numbers/part code are too small and blurred to read beyond a partial '460'.
Photo 1: Close-up of the bell-housing/torque converter mounting face, showing bolt holes and converter splines; no legible part tag visible here either.
Photo 2: Transmission shown from another angle, with dark oil/fluid staining on the wall and ground beneath it, suggesting fluid seepage from the unit or during handling.
No dipstick, wiring harness, or mechatronic/control module clearly visible in any photo.
No video or audio evidence of the unit running, shifting, or being bench-tested.

identity.kind: automatic transmission/gearbox assembly (claimed Mercedes-Benz, possibly 7G-Tronic type)

claims.evidence: No readable part/model plate in any photo; M278 is actually a Mercedes engine code, not a transmission code, raising doubt about the stated identifier.
No video or audio of the unit running or shifting under load.
No odometer, service sticker, or paperwork shown.
Photo 1 shows the bell-housing face exposed but no seal or bolt evidence to confirm it has not been disassembled.
No import documentation, shipping label, or customs marking visible in any photo.

risks.risk: Incorrect or unverified part number could mean wrong application for G63, affecting value and fitment.
risks.proof: Close-up, in-focus photo of the sticker/part plate on the case showing the full alphanumeric code.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unidentified generic automatic transmission core, not as a verified G63-specific unit

risks.risk: Internal wear, burnt clutch packs, or torque converter lock-up solenoid failure not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being bench-tested or installed and shifting through gears.

risks.risk: Fluid leakage visible on the ground in photo 2 could indicate a seal or case crack.
risks.proof: Close-up of the case seams, pan gasket, and output shaft seals showing no active leak.

risks.risk: Missing or damaged mechatronic/control unit, which is costly and integral to 7G-Tronic transmissions.
risks.proof: Photo of the mechatronic unit and wiring connector intact on the transmission.

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit photo of the part/model number plate or stamped code on the transmission case.
Video of the transmission running or shifting on a test bench or installed in a vehicle.
Close-up photos of the case seams and seals to confirm no active fluid leak.
Photo of the mechatronic unit and its wiring harness/connector.
response.reason: The seller's model/part claim cannot be confirmed from any photo since the identifying plate is unreadable, and this code is what determines correct fitment and price tier for a transmission; a legible part-number photo is needed before even a worst-case price can be set.
